gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 independently diagnoses the failure of the claimed functional orthogonality under the stated Chebyshev weight, including the unequal T_0 normalization and an explicit nonzero-inner-product counterexample. Its U005 also recognizes the separate r_ell versus r_ell^0 dimensional/count mismatch noted in the gold. These are distinct manifestations bundled in the gold issue, so the presentation and operation are not identical even though the full substantive concern is recognized.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed orthogonal functional-factor construction is not justified as stated: Euclidean orthogonality of the coefficient columns does not transfer to the Chebyshev-weighted functions because T_0 has a different norm, and the asserted number of functional factors is inconsistent with the dimensions unless additional conditions are imposed.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the prediction uses a different weighted-inner-product demonstration rather than the gold's exact repaired Gram-matrix construction.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of the final weighted orthogonality clause for the functional factors.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the Chebyshev norm mismatch, derives the resulting weighted inner products, gives a nonzero-inner-product counterexample, and proposes weighted normalization or dropping the claim.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed r_ell^0 factor count is inconsistent with the displayed coefficient-factor dimensions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly notes that V has r_ell columns while the statement refers to r_ell^0 polynomials, identifying the same count/dimension inconsistency.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns the total arithmetic complexity claim for the CP-aware RHOSVD method and its omitted spline, DCT, side-matrix SVD, and core-reconstruction terms. ISSUE-005 diagnoses a different estimate for Algorithm 2's full-tensor trivariate spline construction, so it does not recognize the CP-method complexity omission.

The gold identifies a signed-weight error in an absolute-error bound: the triangle inequality requires |xi_k|. ISSUE-004 instead diagnoses missing normalization of spline-interpolant side vectors and the resulting rescaling of CP weights in an RHOSVD estimate. These are different formula and hypothesis failures, even though both alter an error bound involving weights.

Both entries diagnose the same false trivariate full-tensor spline complexity estimate: extrapolating a one-dimensional cost yields a bound smaller than the cost of reading and processing the n^3 input, with cubic n-dependence required.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed O(m^3(m+n)) cost for constructing the trivariate spline from an n_1 by n_2 by n_3 full tensor understates the required input/data-processing cost; in the isotropic case an O(n^3+m^3)-type term is needed.

component_coverage.gold_component: The one-dimensional spline-cost estimate is invalidly extrapolated to the three-dimensional full tensor and omits full-data processing.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly describes Algorithm 2 as operating on the full tensor, requires reading all n^3 entries, and rejects the extrapolated bound as impossible.

component_coverage.gold_component: The corrected complexity must include cubic grid-size dependence and revise the complexity comparison.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the grid-size dependence is cubic rather than linear in n and proposes an O(n^3) or mode-by-mode replacement term.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns malformed cell endpoints, failure of the domain partition, and anisotropic volume normalization in the projection-collocation tensor. ISSUE-002 concerns weighted orthogonality of functional Tucker factors and only shares nearby notation such as r_ell; it provides no diagnosis of the cell indexing or integration formula.
